title: The Wooden Horse
summary: Odysseus' plan that ended the Trojan War: a great wooden horse, built by Epeus with Athena's help, left as a gift with the bravest Greeks hidden inside. The Trojans dragged it into their city and argued over it; that night the Greeks climbed out and sacked Troy.

beats.caption: Built by Epeus, with Athena's help

quote.text: tell us of the wooden horse which Epeus made with the assistance of Minerva

beats.caption: The Trojans drag it into their city

quote.text: the Trojans themselves had drawn the horse into their fortress
What endurance too, and what courage he displayed within the wooden horse

beats.caption: Out of the horse, and Troy falls

quote.text: the sons of the Achaeans issued from the horse, and sacked the town

title: Escaping the Cyclops
summary: Trapped in Polyphemus' cave, Odysseus sharpens an olive stake, tells the giant his name is Noman, blinds him, and escapes clinging under the rams.

beats.caption: An olive stake, hardened in the fire

quote.text: I brought it to a point myself, charring the end in the fire to make it harder
my name is Noman
the men were underneath their bellies
say it was the valiant warrior Ulysses, son of Laertes, who lives in Ithaca

title: The Song of the Sirens
summary: Warned by Circe, Odysseus plugs his crew's ears with wax and has himself bound to the mast so he can hear the Sirens and live.

quote.text: they sit in a green field and warble him to death with the sweetness of their song

beats.caption: Wax for the crew, rope for Odysseus

quote.text: If I beg and pray you to set me free, then bind me more tightly still.
they quickened their stroke

title: Circe's Island
summary: Circe drugs Odysseus' scouts and turns them into pigs; Odysseus resists her spell and she turns them back into men.

quote.text: she drugged it with wicked poisons to make them forget their homes
she turned them into pigs by a stroke of her wand
they became men again, younger than they were before

title: The Bag of Winds
summary: Aeolus ties every storm wind in a bag; within sight of Ithaca, Odysseus falls asleep and his crew open it.

beats.caption: Every wind tied in a sack

quote.text: he flayed me a prime ox-hide to hold the ways of the roaring winds

beats.caption: Home in sight, and so tired

quote.text: I, being then dead beat, fell into a light sleep
They loosed the sack, whereupon the wind flew howling forth

title: The Raft and the Storm
summary: Odysseus builds a raft to leave Calypso; Poseidon sees him and smashes it with a great wave.

beats.caption: A raft, built by his own hands

quote.text: make yourself a large raft with an upper deck that it may carry you safely over the sea
it made him very angry, so he wagged his head and muttered to himself
Neptune sent a terrible great wave that seemed to rear itself above his head

title: Penelope's Web
summary: Penelope holds off the suitors for three years by weaving a shroud by day and unpicking it by night.

beats.caption: Weaving by day, unpicking by night

quote.text: we could see her working on her great web all day long, but at night she would unpick the stitches again by torchlight
She fooled us in this way for three years and we never found her out

title: The Contest of the Bow
summary: Penelope sets a contest: string Odysseus' bow and shoot through twelve axes. Every suitor fails; the beggar strings it with ease.

quote.text: send his arrow through each one of twelve axes
strung it as easily as a skilled bard strings a new peg of his lyre

title: The Olive-Tree Bed
summary: Penelope tests the stranger with the secret of their bed, built around a living olive tree.

beats.caption: A bed no one can move

quote.text: There was a young olive growing within the precincts of the house
I built my room round this with strong walls of stone

title: Athena in Disguise
summary: Athena takes the form of Mentor to guide Telemachus, and gives him courage.

quote.text: Then she took the form and voice of Mentor
she had given Telemachus courage

title: Among the Dead
summary: In the land of the dead, Odysseus tries to embrace his mother's ghost, and Achilles tells him life is worth more than glory.

quote.text: Thrice I sprang towards her and tried to clasp her in my arms
I would rather be a paid servant in a poor man’s house and be above ground than king of kings among the dead
